title: Which Text Matters: Handling Model Uncertainty in Text-as-Data Regressions, with an Application to Central Bank Communication
abstract: arXiv:2610.19720v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Social scientists routinely convert text into covariates like topic shares, ideal points or sentiment scores, and insert them into statistical models of interest. This two-step design is convenient, but it is rarely guided by theory: little tells the analyst which text-based covariates to construct or include. Each approach embodies contestable measurement choices, and competing operationalizations of the same construct can support different conclusions, so a single research question gives rise to a menu of competing regression models. Which text constructed covariates belong in a model, and in what functional form, is thus a problem of model uncertainty. We propose spike-and-slab generalized additive models (SSGAMs), which jointly select covariates and determine whether their effects are linear or nonlinear. We illustrate the approach with the communication of a powerful unelected institution, asking which of 45 competing text indicator

translated_title: 哪些文本才重要：处理文本即数据回归中的模型不确定性——以央行沟通为例的应用
translated_abstract: 社会科学家通常将文本转换为诸如主题份额、理想点或情感得分等协变量，并将其嵌入统计模型中进行分析。这种两步式设计虽然方便，但往往缺乏理论指导：几乎没有依据告诉分析者应当构建或纳入哪些基于文本的协变量。每种方法都涉及存在争议的测量选择，而同一构念的不同操作化方案可能支持不同的结论，因此同一个研究问题会衍生出一整组相互竞争的回归模型。哪些由文本构建的协变量应当被纳入模型，以及应以何种函数形式纳入，由此成为一个模型不确定性问题。我们提出了尖峰-厚板广义可加模型（SSGAMs），该方法能够同时筛选协变量，并判定其效应是线性还是非线性。我们以一个强大的非民选机构的沟通为应用案例，探讨45个相互竞争的文本指标中哪些……
tldr: 本文提出尖峰-厚板广义可加模型（SSGAM），以解决文本构建协变量在回归分析中的模型不确定性问题，可同时自动筛选协变量并判断其效应呈线性还是非线性，并以央行沟通中45个竞争性文本指标的选择为例进行演示。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes spike-and-slab generalized additive models (SSGAMs) to address model uncertainty in text-as-data regressions by jointly selecting which text-based covariates to include and determining whether their effects are linear or nonlinear, illustrated through an application to central bank communication.
